WARDOGS Crashing

A WARDOGS crashing troubleshooting page structure for crash reports, safe checks, and current-build verification.

Target keyword
wardogs crashing
Priority
P0
Manual review
high

Quick Answer

Officially confirmed: BULKHEAD's Closed Beta Known Issues post says crashes are being tracked as part of the test process. The same official post does not provide a universal WARDOGS crash fix.

Use the steps below as general PC troubleshooting, not as WARDOGS-specific official fixes: restart Windows, verify Steam files, update Windows and drivers, close non-essential software, and compare your PC with the Steam system requirements.

If WARDOGS causes a full PC restart, blue screen, or hard freeze, stop treating it like an ordinary game crash. Record the exact symptom, crash report, and time, then wait for official guidance or seek qualified PC support.

Needs Manual Review

Pre-release / Early Access sensitive: This is pre-release / Early Access sensitive content. Current details will be verified against the latest official build before publication.

Before You Try Fixes

  • Officially confirmed:BULKHEAD acknowledged Closed Beta crashes in a pinned Known Issues post and said crash reports help the team catch issues before Early Access launch.
  • Not officially confirmed:No official WARDOGS-specific cause has been published for crashes, driver conflicts, overlays, DirectX errors, Windows updates, or corrupted files in the sources checked on August 28, 2026.
  • Safe generic troubleshooting:Apply general Steam and Windows checks first. Keep a note of what changed so you can reverse it if the issue remains.

Officially Confirmed Crash Issues

  • Officially confirmed:Crashes existed during the Closed Beta and were being tracked by BULKHEAD.
  • Not officially confirmed:No public patch note or official troubleshooting post found in this check names a universal crash fix for WARDOGS.

Safe Troubleshooting Steps

  • Safe generic troubleshooting:Restart Windows and Steam before making deeper changes.
  • Safe generic troubleshooting:Use Steam's Verify integrity of game files tool to check whether installed files are missing or damaged.
  • Safe generic troubleshooting:Update Windows and GPU drivers, then test again with the same settings.
  • Safe generic troubleshooting:Close non-essential overlays, hardware-monitoring tools, recording tools, and background apps for one clean test, but do not permanently disable security software.
  • Safe generic troubleshooting:Compare your PC with the Steam minimum and recommended requirements before assuming the issue is server-side.
  • Safe generic troubleshooting:Check Steam announcements and pinned discussions for current crash notes or patch updates.

Community-reported Crash Patterns

  • Community-reported:Steam Support forum posts describe startup crashes, shader-compilation or DirectX 12 crash reports, and hard crashes during or after entering matches.
  • Community-reported:Some players mention overlays, RGB software, Windows updates, or specific system configurations, but these are mixed reports and should not be treated as universal fixes.

When to Stop Troubleshooting

  • Safe generic troubleshooting:Stop local troubleshooting if the game repeatedly causes a blue screen, full PC restart, or Windows recovery event. Record the crash code or dump evidence instead of repeating the same launch attempts.
  • Safe generic troubleshooting:If many players are reporting the same issue after a new build, wait for an official patch note or developer update before applying risky community workarounds.
